answer: A delta timber exchange could keep an ember of reputation from becoming a bonfire of fake agents by making seller scores non-transferable and granting credit only after independently audited deliveries. Auditors sample shipments after sellers commit, and duplicate delivery IDs earn no extra credit. An attacker must ship real goods or bribe unpredictable auditors to build each alias. Audits cost money, collusion can defeat them, and new honest sellers face a slow start.
